```{r setup}
library(preproSCessR)
library(Seurat)
```

`seuratFrom10x()` handles the two shapes 10x Cell Ranger output actually comes
in -- standard single-sample `cellranger count` runs, and demuxed
`cellranger multi` runs -- behind one interface, so downstream code doesn't
need to branch on which one it's looking at.

You can point it at a single sample or run directly, or hand it a manifest
describing a batch of runs with mixed multiplexing status. Either way, it
returns a named list of Seurat objects, one per sample, ready to merge or
process independently.

## A single, non-multiplexed sample

```{r single-sample}
seurat_list <- seuratFrom10x(
  path        = "/path/to/Sample_1/outs",
  multiplexed = FALSE
)

seurat_list$Sample_1
```

`path` should point to the Cell Ranger `outs/` directory -- the function
looks for `filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5` directly inside it. The sample name
is inferred from the parent folder (`Sample_1`, one level up from `outs`).

## A single multiplexed run

```{r multiplexed-run}
seurat_list <- seuratFrom10x(
  path        = "/path/to/Pool1/outs",
  multiplexed = TRUE
)

names(seurat_list)
#> [1] "Bleo_18_Slim_10" "Bleo_22_Slim_14" ...
```

For `cellranger multi` output, one `outs/` directory contains multiple
demuxed samples under `per_sample_outs/<sample>/`. `seuratFrom10x()` reads
each sample's `sample_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5` separately and returns
one Seurat object per demuxed sample -- a single function call here returns a
list, not a single object.

## A batch of runs via manifest

```{r manifest-batch}
manifest <- data.frame(
  Path = c(
    "/path/to/Sample_1/outs",
    "/path/to/Sample_2/outs",
    "/path/to/Pool1/outs"
  ),
  multiplexed = c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE)
)

seurat_list <- seuratFrom10x(manifest = manifest, min.cells = 3, min.features = 200)
```

The manifest needs a `Path` column (each row's `outs/` directory) and a
logical `multiplexed` column. Rows can mix multiplexed and non-multiplexed
runs freely -- each row is resolved independently, and a multiplexed row
expands into multiple entries in the returned list. If a sample's expected H5
file is missing, that row is skipped with a warning rather than failing the
whole batch; single-path mode fails immediately instead, since there's
nothing left to fall back on.

## Notes

`min.cells` and `min.features` are passed straight through to
`Seurat::CreateSeuratObject()` and apply uniformly across every sample in a
batch -- set them once at the level of granularity you actually want, not
per-sample. The function forces classic (v4-style) Seurat assay objects
internally regardless of which Seurat package version is installed, so
results are consistent even in mixed-Seurat-version environments.
